items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 names the class FarmBlock; the export says so (minecraft:farmland -> ['FarmBlock', 'Block']) but level/classes.rs only knows 'FarmlandBlock', so the chain is [Block] and every farmland arm is dead: farmland_random_tick (tick.rs:350, moisture dry/wet/decay — logic itself verified exact vs FarmBlock.randomTick bytecode), the scheduled-tick arm (tick.rs:197), the survive arm (survive.rs:194), the updateShape arm (shapes.rs:465) and the placement arm (place.rs:922). Farmland never dries, never reverts to dirt. Separately, FarmBlock.fallOn (jar: turnToDirt when an entity falls on it, fall distance > 0.5, random chance, mobGriefing-gated for mobs) has no implementation anywhere in level/ or the game layer — trampling is entirely absent. Latent error in the dead survive arm for the fix agent: the port uses a 'maintains_farmland' tag, but vanilla FarmBlock.canSurvive exempts only a fence gate or moving piston above.
items.title: Farmland is fully static: never dries, never reverts, never tramples (FarmBlock unmapped)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 names the classes SpreadingSnowyDirtBlock and SnowyDirtBlock; the export says so (grass_block/mycelium -> ['GrassBlock'|'MyceliumBlock', 'SpreadingSnowyDirtBlock', 'SnowyDirtBlock', 'Block']; podzol -> ['SnowyDirtBlock', 'Block']) but level/classes.rs only knows 'SpreadingSnowy'/'Snowy', so both names are skipped and the chains are [Grass|Mycelium, Block] / [Block]. The spreading_snowy_tick arm (tick.rs:450 — logic verified faithful vs SpreadingSnowyDirtBlock.randomTick) and the Snowy updateShape arm (shapes.rs:721 — logic verified vs SnowyDirtBlock.updateShape, uses the #snow tag which exists) never run: grass/mycelium never spread to dirt, snowy never updates. Explains the snowy half of pilot failure snowy_grass_and_chests_pair.
items.title: Grass/mycelium never spread; snowy never updates (SpreadingSnowyDirtBlock/SnowyDirtBlock unmapped)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 names the class DirtPathBlock; the export says so but level/classes.rs only knows 'PathBlock', so the chain is [Block] and the Path arms are dead: survive (survive.rs:273), updateShape (shapes.rs:465), tick (tick.rs tick_block Path arm -> turn_to_base_block) and placement (place.rs:929). Port logic verified exact vs DirtPathBlock bytecode (canSurvive: above not solid or fence gate; updateShape schedules tick 1; tick unconditionally reverts to dirt) — dead only due to dispatch. Dirt paths never revert to dirt.
items.title: Dirt path never reverts to dirt (DirtPathBlock unmapped)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 names the classes FungusBlock and RootsBlock; the export says so but level/classes.rs only knows 'NetherFungusBlock'/'NetherRootsBlock', so crimson/warped fungi and roots resolve to Vegetation and survive only on supports_vegetation (#dirt + farmland). Vanilla bytecode: FungusBlock.mayPlaceOn = #NYLIUM || MYCELIUM || SOUL_SOIL || super; RootsBlock.mayPlaceOn = #NYLIUM || SOUL_SOIL || super. Mycelium is already in #dirt, so the gap is nylium + soul soil: fungi/roots cannot be placed on, and pop off, their native Nether ground. Fix note: the port's NetherFungus/NetherRoots may_place_on arm (survive.rs:375) reads data.support_tag, which is None for fungi/roots (they carry requiredBlock instead of supportBlocks in the export), so a mere class-name alias would make survival return false — the fix needs the hardcoded nylium/soul-soil rule.
items.title: Nether fungi/roots cannot survive on nylium or soul soil (FungusBlock/RootsBlock unmapped)

items.evidence: ZERO blocks in the 1.21.7 export carry stemSupportBlocks/supportBlocks/connectsTo/fruitSupportBlocks fields, so support_tag and support_tag2 are None for every block. The Stem/AttachedStem may_place_on arm (survive.rs:375) therefore returns false always, and placement() (place.rs:1595+) refuses any placement that fails can_survive — pumpkin/melon seeds cannot be planted at all. Vanilla StemBlock.mayPlaceOn = is(FARMLAND) (bytecode). The stem_random_tick fruit branch (tick.rs:913) requires support_tag2, so stems never fruit either; vanilla fruits when the target is air and the block below is FARMLAND or #DIRT (bytecode). The stem age-growth branch itself is correct.
items.title: Pumpkin/melon stems cannot be planted and never fruit (no stem support data in the export)

items.evidence: Vanilla CropBlock.getGrowthSpeed is hardcoded: is(FARMLAND) below + MOISTURE > 0 gives 3.0 instead of 1.0 (bytecode-verified), so a hydrated single crop grows ~4x as fast and a hydrated field up to ~9x. The port (tick.rs:819-828) reads tag 'grows_crops', which does NOT exist in 1.21.7 jar data and is NOT synthesized (only data.rs:462 + tick.rs:828 reference it). Growth speed is always 1.0: crops grow ~4x too slow on hydrated farmland.
items.title: Crops grow ~4x too slow: growth speed reads the absent 26.x 'grows_crops' tag

items.evidence: Vanilla MushroomBlock.canSurvive: below in #MUSHROOM_GROW_BLOCK returns true regardless of light, else rawBrightness < 13 and mayPlaceOn (bytecode-verified). The port (survive.rs:266) checks the absent 26.x tag 'overrides_mushroom_light_requirement' instead of 'mushroom_grow_block', which EXISTS in the 1.21.7 jar (mycelium, podzol, crimson/warped nylium) and is in the tags list. Mushrooms on mycelium/podzol/nylium die in bright light where vanilla keeps them.
items.title: Mushrooms die in bright light on mycelium/podzol/nylium (wrong tag name)

items.evidence: Vanilla SnowLayerBlock.canSurvive (bytecode): below in #SNOW_LAYER_CANNOT_SURVIVE_ON (ice, packed_ice, barrier) -> false; in #SNOW_LAYER_CAN_SURVIVE_ON (honey_block, soul_sand, mud) -> true; else isFaceFull(collision, UP) or 8-layer snow below. The port (survive.rs:295) uses the absent 26.x tags 'cannot_support_snow_layer'/'support_override_snow_layer' plus a full-face fallback: snow survives on ice/packed ice/barrier (should pop) and pops on soul sand (should survive; honey/mud pass via the full-face check). The same absent tags are also used in weather.rs:114-117 (snow accumulation) — cross-reference, same fix. The port's full_faces fallback itself matches vanilla's isFaceFull predicate exactly.
items.title: Snow layer survival wrong on ice/packed ice/barrier and soul sand (absent 26.x tags)

items.evidence: Vanilla SeagrassBlock.mayPlaceOn: face sturdy UP and NOT magma block (bytecode-verified hardcoded check). The port (survive.rs:407) checks the absent 26.x tag 'cannot_support_seagrass', so the magma exclusion never fires and seagrass survives on magma blocks.
items.title: Seagrass survives on magma blocks (absent 'cannot_support_seagrass' tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla KelpBlock.canAttachTo: NOT magma block (bytecode-verified hardcoded check). The port (survive.rs:480, growing_plant_can_attach_to) checks the absent 26.x tag 'cannot_support_kelp', so the magma exclusion never fires and kelp attaches to magma blocks.
items.title: Kelp attaches to magma blocks (absent 'cannot_support_kelp' tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla CactusFlowerBlock.mayPlaceOn: below is CACTUS || FARMLAND || isFaceSturdy(UP, CENTER) (bytecode-verified). The port (survive.rs:383) checks the absent 26.x tag 'support_override_cactus_flower' OR face-sturdy-center. Vanilla's own sturdy data (exporter calls state.isFaceSturdy for every state/direction/type) says cactus CENTER_UP is false and farmland CENTER_UP is false, so the port's arm returns false on both: cactus flowers cannot be placed on cacti or farmland, and flowers grown by cactus_random_tick (whose trigger is correct — it checks the cactus's own canSurvive, matching vanilla) pop on the next neighbour update.
items.title: Cactus flowers cannot survive on cacti or farmland (absent 'support_override_cactus_flower' tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla FletchingTableBlock.useWithoutItem returns InteractionResult.PASS (bytecode: getstatic PASS; areturn) — a fletching table has no menu. The port resolves the fletching table to Class::CraftingTable (chain [FletchingTable, CraftingTable, Block] — FletchingTable is unmapped in classes.rs) and the CraftingTable arm (interact.rs:439) returns OpenMenu + Success. Clicking a fletching table opens a crafting menu.
items.title: Fletching table opens a crafting menu (resolves to CraftingTable; vanilla returns PASS)

items.evidence: Every speleothem predicate goes through #minecraft:speleothems (speleothem.rs:15, falling.rs:54-58), a tag absent in 1.21.7 jar data and not synthesized. Vanilla uses hardcoded POINTED_DRIPSTONE checks. speleothem_grow, dripstone_transfer_fluid and spawn_falling_stalactite (its while loop never runs) are all dead: dripstone never grows and stalactites never fall. The randomTick growth chance (0.011377778f) is verified correct in the dead code. The cauldron-fill half is Batch 1's G6 — not duplicated here; this item is growth + falling only.
items.title: Dripstone never grows and stalactites never fall (absent '#speleothems' tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla TreeGrower.growTree removes saplings by setting Blocks.AIR with flags 260 (bytecode-verified). The port's remove_sapling (growth.rs) sets the fluid's legacy block instead — a waterlogged sapling removed for tree growth leaves a water block at the trunk base where vanilla leaves air. The rest of growTree matches vanilla exactly (mega-first with 2x2 fall-through, flower check, weighted feature choice; all ten 1.21.7 growers' feature keys and secondary chances verified against TreeGrower bytecode: oak 0.1, spruce mega 0.5, mangrove 0.85, pale oak mega = PALE_OAK_BONEMEAL).
items.title: Tree growth from a waterlogged sapling leaves water (vanilla sets AIR)

items.evidence: Vanilla SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget returns true unconditionally and AzaleaBlock's likewise; MushroomBlock's returns only whether its feature exists (bytecode-verified). The port's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:331-360) adds growability gates (live features installed + tree_can_grow, which draws random and refuses a lone dark/pale oak sapling with no 2x2) and build-height gates for saplings/azalea/mushrooms. Vanilla consumes bonemeal 45% of the time on an un-growable sapling with no growth; the port refuses the meal outright. The 0.45 success roll itself matches vanilla exactly.
items.title: Bonemeal validity stricter than vanilla for saplings/azalea/mushrooms

The oracle overrides Player.drop with a 3-arg signature (ItemStack, boolean, net.minecraft.util.Prediction); the 1.21.7 jar has only drop(ItemStack, boolean) — the Prediction parameter is a later-version addition. One-symbol repair: drop the third parameter. Blocks test_cauldron_parity.py.
items.title: VanillaCauldronOracle: Player.drop override uses a 3-arg signature 1.21.7 lacks

The oracle calls entity.getRelativePortalPosition(axis, area); the 1.21.7 Entity class has no such method (only portalCooldown/portalProcess accessors). items.evidence: Batch 0 ledger: 1 error, 'cannot find symbol' at line 58. In 1.21.7, DataComponents.BLOCK_ENTITY_DATA is DataComponentType<CustomData> — the BlockEntityData component class does not exist in the 1.21.7 jar at all (introduced in a later version), so data.type() and data.loadInto(entity, access) do not resolve. items.evidence: Batch 0 ledger: 1 error, 'cannot find symbol' at line 36. The oracle uses Feature.DIRECT_CODEC; the 1.21.7 Feature class has no DIRECT_CODEC (only the configuredCodec() instance method). One-symbol repair: decode via the 1.21.7 codec path. Blocks test_replace_block_parity.py.

Cross-references, not re-minted: fire spread ignoring doFireTick (Batch 1 G4); redstone wire arms dead including the dot/cross toggle (Batch 2 G7); dripstone cauldron fill (Batch 1 G6); leaf decay (fixed on main by 5d83cfb8 — not visible in this workdir's files, see source caveat). Owner playtest report 'survival block-breaking drops nothing' (2026-11-22): the level-side drop path (DropResources event + doTileDrops gate, update.rs:445) is verified intact; the symptom is game-layer/loot-side and fixes are underway elsewhere — not duplicated here.
source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 5 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: block ticks, interaction, survival, support, updates, breaking — ~30 drivers; 1,105 blocks grouped by Java class chain. DRAFT: not committed — an execution-risk notice blocks running, building, testing, or issuing git commands inside the repo without the user's go-ahead, so no driver runs, no cargo tests, no oracle repairs, and no commit/push happened in this batch. WORKDIR CAVEAT: the workdir files on disk appear to predate the 14:09 NPT leaf fix (5d83cfb8) and the 14:45 burn fix (a2f95487) — the 12:40 supports synthesis (6e6cb55b) and 11:47 burn-list fix (651b43d3) ARE present, but leaf_distance_at still reads the absent #prevents_nearby_leaf_decay tag with no #logs read and no synthesis, which the leaf fix is recorded as changing. Findings are against the files on disk; the coordinator should re-verify the leaf check against current main on merge. No other finding touches code changed by the leaf or burn fixes.
systemic_note: Two systemic causes cover 11 of the 15 defects. (1) Class-name drift: 28 exported 1.21.7 class names do not map to the port's 26.x-shaped class table (verified exhaustively; Batch 2 verified the same count). Five Batch 5 defects are dead arms behind unmapped names — FarmBlock (B5-G01), SpreadingSnowyDirtBlock/SnowyDirtBlock (B5-G02), DirtPathBlock (B5-G03), FungusBlock/RootsBlock (B5-G04), FletchingTable (B5-G12) — and in every case the port logic itself matches vanilla method-for-method; only the dispatch is dead. (2) 26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in 1.21.7: grows_crops (B5-G06), overrides_mushroom_light_requirement (B5-G07), cannot_support_snow_layer/support_override_snow_layer (B5-G08), cannot_support_seagrass (B5-G09), cannot_support_kelp (B5-G10), support_override_cactus_flower (B5-G11), speleothems (B5-G13) — every lookup silently degrades to the empty set, exactly the pattern behind pilot defects G1/G3/G5/G6. The remaining three are data gaps (no stem support data in the export, B5-G05), a fluid-handling difference (B5-G14) and an over-strict validity gate (B5-G15). The supports_* synthesis (6e6cb55b) is the proven fix pattern for the tag half: chorus, cactus, sugar cane, bamboo, cocoa and vegetation support all pass because their tags are synthesized; the seven defects above are the tags the synthesis does not cover.
